title: A pluggable logger framework
idea: A logger framework turns a log call into a record, drops it if its level is too low, and hands it to appenders that format and write it.
points: `Level` is an `enum`; calls at or above the threshold pass.
Each passing call becomes an immutable `LogRecord` sent to every `Appender`.
An `Appender` decides where output goes; a `Formatter` decides how it looks.
A new destination is a new `Appender` class; `Logger` never changes.

edges.caption: Business code calls `info`; it knows nothing about destinations.
A `debug` call is below INFO, so `log` returns before building anything.
A passing call becomes one immutable `LogRecord`.
`Logger` loops over its appenders and calls `append` on each.
The same record reaches every appender, in list order.

edges.label: format
edges.caption: The console appender asks its `Formatter` for the text, then prints it.

code.title: Logger, appenders, formatter
code.caption: One logger, two appenders. The `DEBUG` call never reaches either.

walk.text: Levels are an `enum` declared lowest first, so `compareTo` orders them.
Two small contracts: how a record looks, and where it goes.
The console appender gets its `Formatter` through the constructor.
`synchronized` keeps the list safe when many threads log at once.
`log` filters by level, builds the record, then fans it out.
`main` wires everything; the logger is configured, never edited.

pitfalls: Check the level before building costly messages; accept a `Supplier<String>` for them.
Catch appender failures inside the logger; a broken disk must not fail checkout.
Make shared appenders thread-safe; every thread writes through the same object.

quiz.q: What is the first line `LoggerDemo` prints?
quiz.why: `DEBUG` is below the `INFO` threshold, so `log` returns early. The `info` call is the first to reach the console appender.

takeaway: Filter by level, build one record, let appenders and formatters do the rest.

starters: How would I add a file appender that rotates files?
Should a logger be a Singleton?
How do I log without slowing down the request thread?
